hens_rule_text: up to 10 female chickens allowed on a single-family lot with a Limited Agriculture Permit, for personal use only; no roosters
permit_notes: A Limited Agriculture Permit from the Durham Planning Department is required. Neighbors are notified during the application; an objection triggers administrative review with the Planning Department making the final call.
setback_notes: Coop must be at least 15 ft from any property line or right-of-way and at least 40 ft from neighboring residences.
coop_rules: Minimum 3 sq ft of floor area per chicken, at least 1 sq ft of window per 15 sq ft of floor area, and chickens must be secured in the coop during non-daylight hours.
zoning_notes: Rule is citywide under Durham Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) Article 5.4.12-B, Domestic Chickens Use Regulations, adopted around 2011 and amended effective Sept. 1, 2017. Selling eggs, chicks, adult chickens, manure or manure-fertilized produce from a permitted flock is prohibited.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

sources.name: Healthy Food Policy Project, Durham N.C. Unified Development Code Sec. 5.4.12 (Sept. 1, 2017)
Growing Food Connections, Domestic Chickens Use Regulations, Article 5.4.12-B of the Durham UDO
INDY Week, Durham says yes to backyard chickens

research_notes: Two independent searches gave matching detail (10 hens, no roosters, Limited Agriculture Permit, 15 ft property-line and 40 ft residence setbacks, coop floor and window standards) from policy-tracker sites that reproduce the UDO section text, but the Durham UDO itself was not opened directly to confirm current wording, so this is treated as a search-extract read of secondary policy summaries of the code.
